_README: Preset for the onset-asynchrony task run as RISING vs NOTHING (seqsfg/asynchrony.py).
Same stimulus machinery and the same Config as asynchrony_config.json -- only the two
task-level choices differ, and only the 'asynchrony' section changes:
orders        ['rising']       one present condition: the element ascends in frequency,
component i starting i*step after the lowest. There is no
order contrast, so the whole session pays for one ladder
and every cell gets twice the trials.
absent_class  'incoherent'     no time-aligned group ANYWHERE. The figure's channels and
the other elements' channels all carry their tones at a
random time inside their own element window. A pure cloud.
Why this absent class, and what it costs. 'roving' (asynchrony_config.json) puts an aligned
group in both classes and varies only whether it recurs, so it is matched at every rung --
but it asks 'did a figure come back', not 'was anything bound'. 'incoherent' asks the
question this project is named after. Synchrony is an envelope event, so it cannot be
envelope-matched, and the size of that cue is largest at 0 ms and gone by the middle of the
ladder. Run `seqsfg asynchrony-verify --preset asynchrony_rising_config.json` and read
section [6]: the rungs where the learnt observer sits at chance are the ones that measure
hearing. Treat 0 ms as a manipulation check, not a data point.
Everything in the 'config' section is identical to asynchrony_config.json, so the two can be
compared rung for rung, and pilot_config.json is untouched by either.
